Subject: Re: Kickoff notes — long-context needs

Thanks for the call this morning, Ava — good overview. Two quick clarifications from our side before we proceed to a short eval:

1) Our primary workload is clinician notes + attachments (PDF snippets) where the useful signal can be 10k+ tokens within a single patient record. We care most about: factual consistency for medication lists, compression/summarization fidelity for handoffs, and extraction accuracy (ICD mapping).

2) Performance sweet spot: we need ~<300ms token latency for interactive triage UI for short replies, but can tolerate higher latency for batch summarization jobs. Cost sensitivity: we are evaluating both hosted and VPC deployment scenarios — please include estimates for both.

Can you send recommended models and a short eval plan (prompt sets + metrics) we can review? Also curious about truncation failure modes you typically see and mitigations.

— Lena
Medical Informatics, CareVault

Subject: Deep-context eval plan and recommended models (preview)

Lena / Marcus — thanks again. Attached is a concise eval plan + sample prompt sets. TL;DR of our recommendations and what we propose to run as a 72-hour pilot: 

- Model shortlist (balanced for quality/latency/cost):
  * redwood-long-7b-ql (our optimized 7B long-context variant) — good tradeoff for interactive use, supports 64k KV cache, expected 120-250ms token latency on Dedicated N5 RTX configs for your median seq lengths.
  * openalt-13b-long-rt (13B q4_0_long) — stronger summarization fidelity on long synth records, ~2-3x cost of the 7B but higher ROUGE / semantic-sim metrics.
  * redwood-30b-quant-long (30B quant) — if you prioritise absolute extraction accuracy and can accept higher latency/cost for batch jobs.

- Truncation modes & failure patterns we see:
  * naive truncation loses trailing context (med list changes late in the record).
  * windowed truncation with static prefix tends to miss early context references.
  * best mitigation: sliding-window KV-cache with periodic intermediate summaries (we propose a 4k stride with 1k overlap + snapshot summaries every 8k tokens). This preserves referential cohesion for both extraction and summarization.

- Suggested evaluation metrics:
  * Extraction: exact match for structured fields (medication, dose) + normalized ICD mapping accuracy.
  * Summarization fidelity: ROUGE-L + embedding-based semantic similarity (cosine on 1536-d embed vectors) against clinician gold summaries.
  * Stability: regression test against a 200-case prompt set (measure hallucination rate per 1k tokens).
  * Latency/cost: per-token latency distributions and per-record cost bucketed by record length.

- Pilot plan:
  * Day 0: deploy two model variants (redwood-long-7b-ql, openalt-13b-long-rt) with KV cache enabled; load 200 representative records (you provide anonymized test subset).
  * Day 1–2: run the prompt sets and collect outputs + embeddings; automated metrics run overnight.
  * Day 3: deliver results CSV + anomaly report + next-step recommendation (canary config for production).

Attachments: sample_prompt_sets.txt (contains representative clinician prompts and edge cases), small_eval_plan.pdf (methodology), preview_results.csv (schema-only preview).

Next steps — what I need from you by Tues: a 200-record anonymized sample (S3 link or Drive), and a short prioritized list of 6 extraction fields. Once we have that, Marissa will spin up the eval harness and Rishi will review model quantization options for VPC pricing.

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync if you want to talk through the config.

— Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Anonymization: our security team requires a noise-injection step and a provenance map. Can Redwood sign an SSA or do you have a standard test-data agreement?
- For the 200 records: acceptable formats? We can provide NDJSON with base64-encoded PDFs.

Folks, quick Q to Marissa/Rishi: from a Dedicated vs VPC pricing standpoint, can you provide a high-level delta (monthly committed baseline) for the two-model pilot vs. going straight to a Dedicated reserved pool? We need an order-of-magnitude for procurement.

— Marcus

Marcus — quick answers and next steps.

1) Data agreement: we have a lightweight test-data addendum used for pilot evals (non-production PII handling + noise steps). I’m attaching the PDF; legal can sign a limited SSA within 48 hours. (attachment: carevault_deep_context_eval_plan.pdf)

2) Formats: NDJSON with base64 PDFs is fine; S3 link preferred. We’ll ingest and run our extractor to verify parsing fidelity.

3) Pricing delta (very high level estimates for budgeting):
   - Pilot (two models, 72 hours, Dedicated burst or Hosted): ~ $6k–$12k depending on throughput and if you use hosted burst capacity. This includes instrumentation + 2 model variants.
   - Small Dedicated reserved pool (monthly baseline to meet interactive SLAs): starting around $22k/month for a small N5 pool with autoscale headroom (regional pricing caveats).
   - VPC private deployment adds per-month infra + setup fee; rough delta of +$8k–$15k/month depending on encryption/keys and HSM integration.

4) Operational recommendation: start with the 72-hour pilot on Hosted or Dedicated burst so we can validate quality. If results show the 13B variant materially improves extraction accuracy (>=5% absolute), we can present a targeted Dedicated sizing + term for procurement.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Marcus: share S3 link to 200 records + prioritized field list (by EOD Wed).
- CareVault sec: review attached test-data addendum and flag any changes.
- Ava/Rishi/Marissa: we'll schedule a 20-min post-pilot review.

I’ll follow up with a short onboarding checklist and a DocuSign for the data addendum.

— Marissa Cole
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
notes: Pilot emphasizes sliding-window KV cache and snapshot summarization to reduce truncation-induced hallucinations.
Evaluation will report both token-latency distributions and per-record cost buckets so CareVault can make a procurement decision informed by both quality and economics.
